A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HLIP research work. All 20 pages of each version, including the appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original HLIP experiments on brain MRI, head CT and chest CT, including benchmark results, ablations, prospective clinical evaluation and computational measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original HLIP experiments and reports additional brain MRI comparisons and zero-shot head CT results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same hierarchical attention procedure, layer allocation, MAE-initialized ViT, positional embeddings and CLS-token propagation. The implementation tables remain unchanged. New comparisons and explanations do not establish a change to HLIP itself.

E1.justification: V2 extends head CT evaluation to zero-shot diagnosis on CQ500 and RSNA, adding a transfer scenario without target-task fitting alongside linear probing. The named datasets, diagnostic targets and prospective cohorts remain unchanged; Pub-Brain-5-GT and its lesion-annotated evaluations already appear in v1.

E2.justification: The brain MRI benchmark comparison expands from BiomedCLIP and ConceptCLIP to include PRIMA and explicit ViT results on both benchmarks (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 1). PRIMA is retrained on BrainMRI220K, adding an important alternative 3D architecture. ViT previously appeared in v1's analyses. Google-CT, FM-HeadCT and the chest CT comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces full-dataset zero-shot head CT evaluation and its inference prompt, and specifies retraining PRIMA using its original recipe. Rad-ChestCT ablations switch from AUC to balanced accuracy (v1 Figure 5; v2 Figure 4). The flash-attention-enabled efficiency condition is removed. The main HLIP training configurations and stated linear-probe protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the data-scale and scan-number sweeps from v1 Figure 4, the training-component and preprocessing ablations in v1 Appendix C/Table 8, and the flash-attention efficiency comparison. Most CLS-token, attention-location, attention-count and batch-size analyses remain, with reorganized presentation and revised chest CT metrics. Figure 1 adds a comparison of naive study-modeling strategies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain throughput estimation using 100 warm-up iterations followed by averaging 1,000 forward passes. V2's added class-average column is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds PRIMA/ViT brain MRI results and head CT zero-shot results. Reported linear-probe margins over FM-HeadCT change from 6.9 to 8.3 AUC points on CQ500 and from 1.4 to 1.7 on RSNA. New zero-shot margins over ViT are 10 and 2.4 points, respectively. Retained HLIP brain MRI scores remain 63.9 on Pub-Brain-5 and 61.3 on Pub-Brain-5-GT; the main chest CT table is unchanged. Scaling, component-ablation and flash-enabled result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of slice, scan and study attention and their I/O and computation-complexity derivations remain unchanged (v1 Appendix E.1; v2 Appendix D.1). No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central claims about HLIP, large-scale uncurated pre-training and cross-modality performance remain. V2 adds public release of the benchmark, implementation, recipe and checkpoints as an explicit contribution and describes training scale in studies rather than patients. Its headline 10.5-point MRI advantage highlights an annotated-subset comparison already reported in v1, replacing the 32.4-point full-benchmark comparison.

C2.justification: V2 expands explanations based on hierarchical priors and discusses study-level curation, broader-organ transfer, future scaling and specialist vision-language models. It removes substantive interpretations concerning MAE initialization, text-encoder overfitting, summarized-report generalizability and possible reasons for glioma underperformance. It also removes the explicit qualification that flash attention reduces HLIP's memory advantage.

D1.justification: V2 adds PRIMA retraining and head CT prompting information, explains the choice of 48 slices using the median, and asserts asset release where v1's discussion promised future implementation/checkpoint release. Removing Appendix C loses the explicit disclosure that the chest CT text encoder is frozen; this does not establish that freezing stopped. Most configuration, hardware and training-time details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 retains the existing references and adds works on PRIMA, transformer information over-squashing and VQ-VAE. These support additional architectural comparisons and motivation, while the general positioning against curated single-scan approaches remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introduction passages are rewritten around uncurated-study modeling. Experiments are reordered to present brain MRI first, ablation discussion is reorganized by component, visualization and clinical evaluation become separate sections, and the final discussion is extensively rewritten. These changes exceed renumbering or isolated language edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the memory comparison with study-modeling comparisons. Figure 3 expands to show zero-shot head CT results, including a combined RSNA display. The MRI table gains comparator rows and a mean column, ablation panels are rearranged with changed axes, and the efficiency table loses its flash-attention columns. Several other figures are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation with domain-trained PRIMA/ViT comparisons and direct zero-shot head CT testing. However, it removes training-component attribution, data-scaling analyses and flash-attention measurements showing when the memory advantage diminishes. These losses weaken transparency and support for the retained mechanism and scalability claims, while the additions improve comparative validation. The competing effects do not establish a reliable net direction in overall paper quality.
